Maintenance Report — MNT-0022-004

Asset: WELL-0022 (SW-23 Well 022, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 12 Apr 2023 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 127 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0022-0024 on 2023-04-06 Report written: 12 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0022-0024 showed the wellhead at 25.2 °C with the air at 21.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,765
Bolts, shims and seals441
Bearing grease and consumables736
Labour (company crew and contractor)3,507
Total6,449

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten the same day as the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0022-017

Asset: WELL-0022 (SW-23 Well 022, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 20 Jul 2025 08:00 · Finished: 13 Aug 2025 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 575 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0022-0139 on 2025-07-17 Report written: 15 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0022-0139 showed the wellhead at 32.3 °C with the air at 32.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

V-belts766

Labour (company crew and contractor)3,158

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0022-024

Asset: WELL-0022 (SW-23 Well 022, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Oct 2026 08:00 · Finished: 02 Oct 2026 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 14 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0022-0195 on 2026-10-01 Report written: 02 Oct 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0022-0195 at 15:45 on 2026-10-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.1% of the pad area, estimated 4.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 222 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 178 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0022-024 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.6% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
